claim: fork() write-protects the PTEs of private writable mappings in both parent and child (copy_present_pte); the first write then takes a write-protect fault handled by do_wp_page -> wp_page_copy (inlined in this build), which gives the writer a fresh physical page while the other process keeps the original. Shared mappings are never write-protected — fork does not even copy their PTEs — so no copy ever occurs there.

evidence.output_excerpt:
do_wp_page fired: pid=184 addr=0x100000000000

        do_wp_page+1
        __handle_mm_fault+2133
        handle_mm_fault+323
        do_user_addr_fault+352
        exc_page_fault+103
        asm_exc_page_fault+38
evidence.interpretation: The write-protect fault handler fires exactly once, in the child (pid 184), at the mapped page, reached from the page-fault entry path. wp_page_copy has no kallsyms entry in this build (inlined into do_wp_page, its only caller), so the copy itself is proven by the pagemap evidence below, not by this probe.

evidence.command: /tmp/cow-trigger private (reads /proc/self/pagemap in parent and child before/after the child's single write; see guest/cow-trigger.c)
evidence.output_excerpt:
parent_pfn_before=0x1323a
child_pfn_before=0x1323a
child_minflt_delta=1
child_pfn_after=0x143ad
parent_pfn_after=0x1323a
parent_reads=0xa5
evidence.interpretation: One physical page (PFN 0x1323a) is shared by both processes after fork; after the child's write the child maps a new page (0x143ad) while the parent keeps the original. The write cost exactly one minor fault, and the parent's sentinel (0xa5) is untouched — memory isolation held.

evidence.output_excerpt:
parent_pfn_before=0x855d
child_pfn_before=0x0
child_present_before=0
child_minflt_delta=1
child_pfn_after=0x855d
parent_reads=0x5a
evidence.interpretation: For a shared mapping fork copies no PTEs at all (child PTE non-present); the child's write takes one minor fault that maps the parent's page — same PFN, do_wp_page silent, write visible to the parent. This distinguishes COW from both fault noise and ordinary lazy population.
Fork side: for COW-eligible mappings (is_cow_mapping && pte_write), ptep_set_wrprotect() on the parent and pte_wrprotect() on the child's copy — the arming of COW.
Fault side: handles the write to a write-protected PTE; for a page still shared with the other process it falls through to wp_page_copy.
Allocates the new page, copies contents, and re-maps the faulting PTE writable. Inlined into do_wp_page in this build (no kallsyms entry).
Why the shared-mapping control behaves as observed: fork skips PTE copying entirely for VMAs with no anon_vma, so shared mappings are lazily re-faulted, never write-protected.

expected: probe do_wp_page fires exactly once, under the child PID, at address 0x100000000000, via handle_mm_fault (private)
parent and child PFNs equal before the write; child PFN changes across the write; parent PFN does not (private)
child minor-fault delta across the single write == 1 (private)
parent sentinel reads 0xa5 after the child's write (private; isolation)
probe silent; child PTE non-present at fork; child faults in the parent's PFN; parent reads 0x5a (shared control)
repro.tolerance: exact (PFN values vary per boot; assertions compare equality/inequality between readings, never absolute values)

limitations: THP is not exercised (single 4 KiB page; the huge-page path do_huge_pmd_wp_page differs). wp_page_copy is claimed via caller probe + PFN divergence because it is inlined in this build. Minor-fault exactness relies on the trigger's warmed measurement window; see guest/cow-trigger.c.
